title: Aleppo Pine: Old Aleppo Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: Its cones open in fire, so the blaze that kills the tree sows the next one. Canberra's Lone Pine grew from a cone carried home from Gallipoli.
intro: An Aleppo pine keeps its cones locked shut on the branch for years and opens them with heat, so the fire that kills the tree sows the next generation of it. It is the pine of the Mediterranean's dry hillsides, and the old ones mostly stand where somebody decided to keep them. Nice owes a whole forest to it: when the city became French in 1860 the slopes of Mont Boron were bare rock, and the replanting begun in 1862 is the pine wood you walk through today. Trieste's Miramare park protects six within three hundred metres of each other. Bari's Pine of Carrassi is close to six metres round, though one botanical survey calls it a stone pine. And in Canberra the Lone Pine of the Australian War Memorial grew from a cone a sergeant picked up at Gallipoli in 1915 and carried home.
